source.display_title: 05/28/2026 - Gökmen Toroslu x Harry Edmonds  — Follow Up

setter.name: Kyla
setter.evidence: "Kayla, not Kayla, uh... Kyla, yeah, she said she was in England, too" and "she was very helpful. We were, like, talking for at least half an hour, going over stuff." The rep confirms the relationship: "She's actually my girlfriend, yeah." No setter code appears in the title.

prospect.name: Gökmen Toroslu
prospect.aka: James — the only name used on the call, by both parties ("Be real with me, James"). The transcript speaker label is also James. The title name and the in-call name do not match; see the flags file.
prospect.location: Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, New York, USA; also owns rental property upstate New York
prospect.occupation: Former union steamfitter in New York City for around 25 years, now in project management. Co-owns a company with partners, freelances project management for two other companies, and runs short-term rental property upstate.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife is 41 and a stay-at-home parent who trains with a private coach at $700/month. One daughter, aged 10, who spends summers in Italy with her grandparents. Italian in-laws visiting at the time of the call. Twenty years sober.
prospect.training_background: Physically strong from decades of manual trade work, now largely desk-bound in project management. Trains at least three times a week in a home gym he and his wife built out — sauna, cold plunge, Smith machine, cable machine, lat pulldown, kettlebells. Runs twice a week, anywhere from two to ten miles, and rates his cardio as excellent. Bought Trevor's kettlebells and follows his content, saving reels and assembling his own routines. Held a $59/month gym membership in Brooklyn for roughly fifteen years and almost never went; cancelled it after building the home gym.
prospect.medical: Nothing disclosed and nothing asked. Reports twenty years of sobriety from alcohol and drugs. Speculates about "possible metabolism slowing down". No injuries, conditions, medications or clinician mentioned by either party at any point.

signals: Successful in every domain except this one and explicit about it: "I've accomplished and succeeded in so many things in life, um, except me. Physically" and "this is the one area I'm lacking"
Price read as reasonable against an existing benchmark rather than as a barrier: "That's not terrible. My wife pays 700 a month for her guy"

Self-scored 6.5-7 out of 10 and wants definition rather than rescue — "I want to just be able to wear a nice t-shirt and, I'm not flexing or anything, but you can kind of see, hey, this guy's taking care of himself"

goals.text: Visible muscle definition — look like someone who takes care of himself in a t-shirt
Confidence in front of his family, particularly on the beach with his wife and daughter
Mobility work for joints and tendons he does not otherwise use, because of his age
Stop the decline before it starts — "I don't want to all of a sudden, just like, next thing you know, it's like, just downhill"
A structured regimen with protected time for himself amid a very heavy workload
Get his nutrition and protein intake right after years of not doing it
Keep pace with a wife who is in excellent shape and looks a decade younger

pains.text: Fifteen years of paying for a gym membership he almost never used — "you've been donating to the gym because I never go"
Cannot make the decision to prioritise himself — "I won't make the determined decision to say, okay, this is it"
Work displaces everything; too many businesses and roles, "my head's spinning constantly because I've just taken so much on"
Has conquered poverty, addiction and business but not this — "I've conquered so many demons outwardly... except me. Physically"
Embarrassment about how he looks next to his wife and daughter
Belly fat and no definition despite genuine strength
Cannot build a coherent programme from saved reels — "trying to kind of create my own kind of workout strategies... It is difficult"
Has not been hitting protein targets for years

objections.raw_quote: All right, so let's do this. Let me speak to my wife and tell her that my trainer is going to be more than hers. See her reaction, let her cool off, and then, you know, we can probably do this. I don't see an issue why I can't.
objections.rep_response: Ran most of the OB play. Tested whether her answer would actually change anything ("What if she doesn't [agree]?" — "she will, she doesn't have a choice"), challenged the necessity directly ("Can I challenge you? Do you really need to speak to her?"), pushed for the real hesitation twice, and finished with the scripted deposit fallback: a $100 refundable deposit, taken live by Stripe link.

objections.raw_quote: six grand, it's, it's, it's a bit much, but I think I can do it and convince her to let me do it... If it was like two, three grand, I'd be like, alright, but, you know, let me speak to her.
objections.rep_response: Pre-empted the number before quoting it — "Can I ask you a question? What if it doesn't fit in the budget? What happens then?" — which surfaced his own ceiling ("if it's a couple grand, it's not a problem") before the price landed. After the quote he did not defend price at all; the prospect resolved it himself against his wife's trainer at $700/month. No financial picture was taken.

objections.raw_quote: No, let's see. Let's see. Let's see. Let's see what happens here. Let me speak to my wife, work thing, you know, make sure this is the right thing.
objections.rep_response: Refused to accept the soft answer and said so: "So there is something coming up. Be real with me, James. Just be real" and later "what's really coming up for you, man? Cause I know you need to speak to her. If she says no, you'll do it anyway. Like what's really coming up for you?"

offer.payment_plan_terms: None discussed. A $100 refundable deposit was taken by Stripe link to hold the following day's call, described by the rep as standard practice for follow-ups.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "We will guarantee the results. We'll put our money where our mouth is. So we'll guarantee you that you'll get 20 pounds on all your moves with the kettlebell by the end of it... 20 pounds on the kettlebell weight that you use... And we guarantee that, or we work with you for free until you get there. So you know you're paying for the outcome." The prospect initially misheard it as 20 lb of muscle and the rep corrected him immediately.

evidence: No agreement to purchase. Asked directly whether he was all in, he twice gave a soft answer: "Yeah, I think so, man" and "I think so. I think we can do this, dude"
Explicitly deferred pending his wife: "Let me speak to my wife and tell her that my trainer is going to be more than hers... and then, you know, we can probably do this"

A $100 refundable deposit was paid live by Stripe link and confirmed received ("That just came through, by the way, I saw that"), but it holds a call rather than a programme — the rep stated three times it was refundable
A follow-up call was booked for 3pm Eastern the next day, at which the prospect said he would give his answer

Counter-evidence pointing toward a likely close: strong intent language ("this would change my life, dude. Straight up"), price accepted against his wife's $700/month trainer, a payment method already chosen (a new Amex Delta SkyMiles Platinum, for the miles), and "I don't see an issue why I can't. There's no reason."
The programme itself was not paid for, no payment link for the $6,000 was sent, and no onboarding call with Trevor was booked
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call with the rep at 3pm Eastern the next day, after the prospect speaks with his wife; onboarding with Trevor pencilled for the following Monday if it converts

notable.note: The best-qualified prospect and the best-run discovery in the batch, and it still did not close on the call. Three things for a principal. First, the name on the file does not match the name used on the call — the title says Gökmen Toroslu and both parties say James throughout — which puts the identity of a live deal in question. Second, a $100 deposit was taken by Stripe link, and the rep described it as standing policy: "this is what we do when we schedule follow-ups. We always take a hundred dollar deposit." No other follow-up in this batch involved a deposit, including three booked in the previous fortnight, so either the policy is new or it is not a policy. Third, the setter on this call is the closer's girlfriend, which he disclosed unprompted and then used for rapport ("Kyla told me that she was excited for me to speak with you") — worth knowing as a governance fact rather than as misconduct. Also notable: this is the only call in the batch where anything resembling a consequence frame ran, and the only one where the rep refused to accept a soft yes.

quality.notes: Severe and continuous inversion — this is the worst-labelled file in the batch. Whole rep passages sit under the James label (the entire offer walkthrough from 00:25:11, "Once that's out the way, cool. All we need to do at that point is create a program and reverse engineer everything"; the guarantee at 00:31:44; "but yeah, it's six grand for the six months" at 00:32:11) and many of the prospect's lines sit under Harry Edmonds, including "What would change if you had that?" which is plainly the rep. The speaker label is James throughout while the file title names Gökmen Toroslu. Roles were read entirely from content.
